newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Qatar's emir willing to visit Bahrain - paper.
newsitem.headline: Qatar's emir willing to visit Bahrain - paper.

text.p: Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani said in remarks published on Monday he was ready to visit Bahrain to persuade it not to boycott Saturday's Gulf Arab summit.

"If my brothers in Bahrain would agree, I have no objection to go in person to Bahrain to invite (Bahrain's) Sheikh Isa (bin Sulman al-Khalifa) to attend the Gulf summit," Kuwait's al-Qabas newspaper quoted Sheikh Hamad as saying.

Bahrain said on Wednesday it would not attend the summit in Qatar, which has taken a territorial dispute with the island state to the International Court of Justice. The move has angered the island state of Bahrain which insists on a Gulf Arab solution.

The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) -- an economic and political alliance which groups Oman, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates -- is to hold its annual summit in the Qatari capital of Doha on December 7.
"We are keen on Bahrain attending the Doha summit and we will exert our utmost effort so that Bahrain participates," Sheikh Hamad said in an interview with the Arabic daily.

Qatar and Bahrain are locked in a territorial dispute over a group of barren islands, reefs and sandbanks which are potentially valuable and of strategic importance. They have been controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s.
Bahrain said on Monday it had arrested two Qataris on charges of spying for Qatar, a small peninsula on the east coast of Saudi Arabia.
"In case Saudi Arabia reaches a solution that satisfies both sides the case would be withdrawn (from the International Court of Justice)," Sheikh Hamad added.
Bahrain's Cabinet Affairs and Information Minister Mohammad Ibrahim al-Mutawae said on Thursday Manama might attend the summit if the problems prompting its boycott were removed.
The secretary-general of the GCC Jameel Hujilan said on Sunday he was optimistic Bahrain would reconsider its decision.

GCC leaders have been trying to persuade Bahrain to drop its threat to boycott the summit. Qatar has said it would only withdraw the case if mediation by Saudi Arabia, the region's dominant power, was successful.
